title: red-server
description: red-server — a Proxmox node, on its own hardware at 192.168.70.13.

options.content:
**red-server** · `192.168.70.13` · role `hypervisor` · a Proxmox node, on its own hardware.  
Eight tiles, then one section per resource. Use **Nodes** in the header to jump to another host.

---

panels.title: Reachable
panels.description: Whether Prometheus got a scrape, which is not the same as the workload being healthy.

panels.title: Load per core
panels.description: Runnable processes divided by cores. Above 1 means work is queueing.

targets.expr: node_load1{host="red-server"} / on (host) group_left () count by (host) (count by (host, cpu) (node_cpu_seconds_total{host="red-server"}))

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Against MemAvailable, so page cache is counted as free — which it effectively is.

panels.title: Swap in use
panels.description: Any swap in use on a host with RAM to spare is worth a look; sustained growth is a leak.

panels.title: CPU package
panels.description: At the die. Intel reports it as Package id 0, AMD as Tctl.

targets.expr: max(node_hwmon_temp_celsius{host="red-server"} * on (host, chip, sensor) group_left (label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{label=~"Package id 0|Tctl"} * 9 / 5 + 32)

options.content:
Where the time goes, and whether anything is waiting for it.

---

panels.title: CPU by mode
panels.description: Normalised to one core's worth, so the stack tops out at 100% however many cores the host has. A tall iowait band is a disk problem wearing a CPU costume.

targets.expr: sum by (mode) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{host="red-server", mode!="idle"}[$__rate_interval])) / on () group_left () count(count by (cpu) (node_cpu_seconds_total{host="red-server"})) * 100

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: The flat line is the core count. Load above it means the run queue is longer than the machine is wide.

panels.title: CPU pressure
panels.description: Share of time at least one task was runnable but waiting for a core. This is the honest measure of CPU contention; utilisation is not.

panels.title: Clock speed
panels.description: Cores parked at the floor under load mean thermal or power limiting.

options.content:
Where the RAM went. Cache is not a leak.

---

panels.title: Memory breakdown
panels.description: Stacked to total RAM. Only the blue band is memory a process actually holds.

panels.title: Memory pressure
panels.description: Time spent reclaiming rather than working. Non-zero here, before the OOM killer runs, is the early warning.

panels.title: Major page faults
panels.description: Faults that had to go to disk. Sustained non-zero means the working set no longer fits.

options.content:
Physical devices as this host sees them. These are the physical drives in the machine.

---

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Reads above the line, writes below it.

panels.title: Utilisation
panels.description: Share of wall time with at least one request in flight. Sustained 100% is saturation.

panels.title: I/O pressure
panels.description: Time tasks spent blocked on storage.

options.content:
Physical and bridge interfaces. Container veths and Proxmox firewall bridges are filtered out.

---

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Inbound above the line, outbound below it.

panels.title: Errors and drops
panels.description: Flat zero is the healthy shape.

panels.title: TCP retransmits
panels.description: Retransmits against total segments sent. The ratio is what matters, not the count.

panels.title: Connection tracking table
panels.description: Filling this table makes the host drop new connections without logging anything useful.

options.content:
Sensors and drives that belong to this physical machine.

---

panels.title: Temperatures
panels.description: Package first, then each core. The four Intel nodes report per-core sensors as `Core N`; grey-server is AMD and reports one per-die sensor, `Tccd1`, so both are matched. node_hwmon reports Celsius, so the query converts and the thresholds move with it — changing only the display unit would label a Celsius number as Fahrenheit.

targets.expr: node_hwmon_temp_celsius{host="red-server"} * on (host, chip, sensor) group_left (label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{label=~"Package id 0|Tctl"} * 9 / 5 + 32

panels.title: SMART
panels.description: Only the attributes every drive here reports. Pending sectors and UDMA CRC errors are ATA attributes the Samsung SSD in purple-server does not expose, so they live on [Storage & Drive Health](/d/storage-health) instead. The NVMe controller reports no overall self-assessment, so its row reads `not reported`; its health is in the NVMe table above.

options.content:
What this node is actually carrying.

---

panels.title: Guests on red-server
panels.description: Joined against pve_guest_info filtered to this node, so only this node's guests appear.

defaults.noValue: No guest is registered on this node.

targets.expr: pve_up{id=~"(qemu|lxc)/.*"} * on (id) group_left (name, node, type) pve_guest_info{node="red-server"}

panels.title: Guest CPU on red-server
panels.description: Top eight guests on this node.

options.content:
This node is read by the NUT server for ups01. Full detail on [Power & UPS](/d/power-ups).

---

What this machine is, and the housekeeping nobody looks at until it matters.

panels.title: Clock offset
panels.description: Against the NTP source. A drifting clock quietly ruins every graph on this page.

defaults.noValue: No unit is in the failed state.
